newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Jan 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Germany's Marc-Kevin Goellner failed to upstage top seed Goran Ivanisevic in an opening round match of the Sydney International tennis tournament at White City yesterday. Despite acing Ivanisevic 15 to eight, Goellner lacked the control needed to piece together his game to beat the Croat. Page 16.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor has made it clear that playing well in the fourth Test is more important than making the one-day finals later this month, reinforcing the focus of Australian cricketers. Australia will struggle to make the limited-oers play-off if they fail to beat Pakistan in Hobart today, but a draw in Adelaide will be enough for Australia to retain the Frank Worrell Trophy. Page 16.

1996 Olympic sailing coach Mike Fletcher has warned against complacency in the lead-up to the 2000 Olympics. Fletcher has raised concern over the growing idea that Australia will do well in Sydney because the sailors are familiar with the Harbour current and wind shifts and because they won medals at Savannah and believes the top Olympic teams will be arriving in Sydney over the next year and will soon know more about the Harbour's wind and currents than any local. Page 14.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Greg Norman won $US1 million (A$1.25m) over two days in the Arizona desert at the weekend, after beating American Scott Hoch one up in the 36-hole final of the Andersen Consulting world championship of golf. In the one match Norman collected $108,763 moe than he did playing 17 tournaments on the US circuit in 1996 and his previous biggest prize cheque totalled just $US450,000 for winning the 1994 US players championship. Page 44.

World Number three and top seed at the Sydney International, Goran Ivanisevic, credited as having the game but not the brain to be a Wimbledon Champion and world number one, claims his days of violent outbursts are over. The 25-year-old Croat was a mode of decorum at the White City match yesterday against Germany's Marc-Kevin Goellner and credits his boyhood friend and coach Vedran Martic as the man who's taught him to manage his temper. Page 44.

Stuart Law looks likely to become Australia's number three batsman for the Adelaide Test on Australia Day. Law has proven himself on limited-overs level hitting 76 from 100 balls against Pakistan for Australia A in Sydney and 93 from 107 balls for Australia against the West Indies. Law is expected to surpass injured Victorian player Matthew Elliott, Matthew Hayden and Justin Langer. Page 43.
THE AGE

The national jockeys' dispute flared up yesterday as interstate stewards handed out heavy fines to those refusing to ride on Saturday and Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett gave his support to the jockeys' pay claims. While Sydney jockeys were fined A$500 fo each ride missed at Randwick and A$300 a ride for the provincial meeting at Kembla Range, Victorian jockeys met at Flemington to reaffirm their support for the national pay claims. Page C6.

Australia's Wimbledon semi-finalist Jason Stoltenberg has withdrawn from the Colonial Classic and the Ford Australian Open because of swollen tendons in his forearm just above the wrist. Stoltenberg is due to undergo corrective surgery this morning and is expected to be out of action for a month - meaning a miss in the Davis Cup tie against France in Sydney early next month. Page C6.

World Cup winning coach Dav Whatmore believes the Australian team's tentativeness and introspection has brought the four consecutive defeats that have led Australia back to the field in Test and one-day series. The former Victorian and Australian batsman believes the game of cricket is 90 per cent psychological and that the Australian team has not been properly prepared. Page C6.
THE HERALD SUN

Melbourne has beaten Sydney in the battle to host the prestigious international golf event the President's Cup. Melbourne's sandbelt has secured the Australasian PGA Tour to be held late next year following six weeks of discussion with US counterparts. The venue has been narrowed down to Royal Melbourne or Kingston Heath - which Australian officials are believed to favour. Page 72.

Victorian jockeys may yet join the Australian Workers Union (AWU) as they stand firm over their campaign for a national riding fee. Victoria's Jockeys' Association president Neville Wilson, one of more than 40 of the State's leading riders who met yesteray to support the push for a national A$130 riding fee, said they were committed to the National Jockey Council. Page 70.

West Indies batsman Carl Hooper finally looks set to fulfil his immense potential following his matchwinning 110 not-out performance against Australia in Brisbane on Sunday night. Hooper is now the tour's leading run-getter with 778 in all matches at an verage of 48.6, which includes Test and one-day centuries. Page 66.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Norths president Ray Beattle said last night that any decisions the Bears' Board makes regarding the behaviour of several North Sydney players at a day-night cricket game last week will not be made public. ARL chief Ken Arthurson is set to impress upon Nrth officials the need for a public statement given the publics' knowledge of the players' misconduct. Page 58.

The Australian Workers Union which represents the racing industry, began talks yesterday with the jockey associations aimed at establishing an industrial alliance. The AWU believes the alliance will be able to begin pressuring racing clubs in a few days to drop fines imposed on jockeys yesterday and begin talks on pay claims. Page 57.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor believes Australia may be in danger of missing the finals if they fail in the one-day match against the unpredictable Pakistan team at the Bellerive Oval today. A defeat would have the West Indies and Pakistan sharig top spot on the ladder with three wins from five games and Australia with two from six and two to play. Page 55.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
